units.content: Models alignment through common-goal/attractor dynamics across interacting intelligent systems.
Goals are represented as attractors/basins that can organize trajectories; alignment is framed as preserving coherent movement toward shared or compatible attractors.
Source proposes that stronger common attractors/feedback should reduce drift and improve coordination among adapting subsystems.
Conceptual alignment model, not an empirically established attractor law.
Proposes criteria for identifying an AGI-like transition as a change in improvement dynamics rather than a score threshold.
Candidate criteria include generator self-improvement, reachability expansion, capability acceleration, transfer, self-evaluation and preserved alignment/truth coupling.
Distinguishes ordinary scaling from a phase transition by requiring longitudinal and causal evidence about generator change under controlled resources.
Candidate phase-transition criteria; no AGI transition is reported as observed.
Proposes an observatory for longitudinally measuring candidate AGI-transition variables.
Proposes dashboards/channels for generator change, capability, reachability, alignment, resource controls and transition signatures.

This layer uses Omega as a source-local acceleration quantity based on change in capability growth, including Omega=Delta(Delta C)/Delta t; identity with earlier Omega=dG_m/dt is not asserted by the compressor.
Contains example/mock observatory values and language such as approaching a transition; these are illustrative display states, not measured observations.
Measurement-system proposal with mock/example output; no live observatory execution or result artifact is present.
Proposes an engineering architecture intended to produce AGI-like recursive improvement.
Specifies candidate representation, world/self-model, search/generator, evaluator, memory, interface and alignment/control components connected in recursive improvement loops.
AGI-like behavior is predicted to require autonomous improvement of improvement mechanisms rather than only higher task performance.
Engineering design hypothesis, not an implemented AGI system.
Proposes safety/control mechanisms for recursively improving intelligence.
Candidate safeguards include monitoring, validation, sandboxing, rollback, constraint boundaries, adversarial testing, alignment feedback and preserved reality contact.
Capability growth alone is not treated as safe progress; control/evaluation capacity must remain coupled to change in system capability.
Safety architecture proposal; no safety guarantee or executed control test is established.
Defines candidate evaluation tests for AGI-like recursive intelligence.
Evaluation covers representation discovery, generator improvement, reachability expansion, longitudinal capability, self-evaluation/alignment and resource-controlled comparisons.
Contains illustrative scoring/bar-style evaluation examples; these are not observations of a tested system.
Evaluation protocol proposal; AGI evaluation result = NOT_REPORTED_ON_THIS_SOURCE.
Organizes an AGI research program around falsifiable questions rather than capability scaling alone.
Proposes coordinated tracks for representation, generator improvement, evaluation, reachability, alignment, interfaces, multi-agent/civilization systems and empirical tests.
Emphasizes baselines, controls, longitudinal trajectories, ablations and explicit failure criteria.
Research roadmap/program, not a record of completed experiments.
Proposes a minimal seed architecture from which recursive intelligence might emerge.
Candidate minimal components include reality/world representation, self-model/evaluation, improvement generator, memory, feedback and alignment/control loops.
The source proposes that a sufficiently small set of recursive/evaluative components may be enough to cross from fixed learning into autonomous generator improvement.
Minimal-seed hypothesis/proposal; no seed implementation or demonstrated emergence is reported.
Models possible dynamics if recursive intelligence begins accelerating its own improvement process.
Distinguishes capability level, capability velocity and recursive improvement dynamics; explores feedback loops in which improved intelligence improves the mechanisms generating further intelligence.
Uses velocity/acceleration style quantities and generator-change relations to describe saturation, bounded acceleration or runaway regimes.
Possible dynamical regimes/theory; no singularity trajectory is observed or predicted with calibrated probability.
Extends alignment/control analysis to civilization-scale human, AI, institutional and technological systems.
Models distributed objectives, institutions, coordination, feedback and shared reality/representation layers as components of civilization-scale alignment.
Local optimizer alignment does not automatically imply coherent system-level trajectories; coordination and feedback become explicit bottlenecks.
Civilization-scale alignment theory/proposal, not a validated governance architecture.
Generalizes the framework across biological, artificial, collective and civilizational substrates.
Source proposes that different substrates may instantiate a common adaptive intelligence pattern involving representation, feedback, transformation, improvement and reachability.
Presents source-local universal intelligence coordinates/functions intended to abstract away from substrate-specific implementation.
Universalization hypothesis/framework; universality is not empirically established by the layer title.
Explores whether causal influence/intelligence effects obey a conservation-like principle across transformations.
Causal mass is represented through counterfactual dependence/persistence of future trajectories on a system, intervention or representation.
Proposes a conservation-like relationship for intelligence/causal influence rather than stating an established conservation law.
The source explicitly marks the conservation principle as speculative/hypothetical.
Use of conservation terminology and equations does not grant physical-law standing.
Explores a field-style representation of distributed intelligence/influence.
Introduces source-local field, density, flow/gradient and interaction concepts for describing distributed transformation potential.
Treats intelligence as potentially distributed across agents, interfaces and environments rather than confined to a single object.
Conceptual field theory; no measured physical/intelligence field is reported.
Explores thermodynamic/resource constraints on intelligence and transformation.
Introduces source-local resource/energy, entropy/uncertainty, efficiency, transformation budget and related thermodynamic analogies.
Proposes that intelligence/reachability expansion is constrained by resource costs and efficiency tradeoffs rather than being unconstrained.
Presents conceptual equations relating transformation capacity, resource boundaries, compression and reachable-state expansion.
Thermodynamic framework/hypothesis, not a demonstrated thermodynamic law of intelligence.
Proposes a unified equation for intelligence evolution across multiple framework components.
Uses a source-local intelligence state including representation quality, generator improvement, reachable possibility space, capability, causal influence/alignment and related coordinates.
Proposes a dynamical relation in which representation/generator changes and constraints alter future intelligence/reachability trajectories.
In this layer R denotes representation quality/state; this local definition must not be merged with earlier uses of R for resources.
Proposed unifying equation, not empirically fitted or proved.
Proposes empirical measurement channels for intelligence evolution, generator improvement and phase transitions.

Channels cover representation quality, generator change, reachable frontier, capability, causal mass, alignment, resource controls, generator ablation, acceleration, novelty, compression, interface effects and civilization-level measurement.
A candidate transition should show generator change -> acceleration -> reachability expansion -> capability change rather than resource scaling alone.
Failure conditions include capability acceleration without generator change, generator change without reachability effect, representations not improving search and causal mass being unmeasurable.
Measurement protocol; proposed tests/proxies are not validated measures and no data are reported.
Designs feedback systems intended to preserve objectives/coherence during intelligence acceleration.
Defines source-local alignment state A=(O,M,F,R), alignment gradient/bandwidth, drift and attractor/basin concepts; local R means robustness here.
Proposes monitor-model-correct-verify loops and continuous alignment feedback rather than a one-time constraint.
Well-aligned adaptive systems are predicted to increase capability/generator quality/alignment while decreasing drift; danger arises when capability changes faster than alignment feedback.
Control architecture/theory; inequalities such as Delta A >= Delta C are design hypotheses, not observed invariants.
Defines a candidate boundary between ordinary learning and recursive improvement.
A recursive boundary is proposed when Delta G_m>0 is caused by the system itself; resource scaling or ordinary capability gains do not satisfy the criterion.
Proposes equal-resource comparison of fixed-generator and self-improving-generator systems with longitudinal acceleration measurement.
Boundary criterion/hypothesis; no recursive system crossing is reported.
Proposes a minimal architecture capable of recursive intelligence improvement while preserving alignment.
Proposed stack includes world model, self model, generator, evaluator, alignment controller, memory/interface and a closed improvement loop.
AGI-like transition is hypothesized to require self-modeling, improvement search, reliable evaluation and continuous control, not merely larger model capability.
Distinguishes powerful fixed optimizers, recursive-but-unstable systems and blind recursion as different failure classes.
Architecture hypothesis only; no AGI implementation or validation is present.
